permit.applies: The worker, or an authorised person on the worker's behalf (a travel agent, a cruise ship operator, a family member), through the online portal.
permit.first: Details of the contract or other arrangement under which the work will be done, and the health insurance the Ordinance requires.
permit.exemptNote: None for performers: under Schedule 2 of the Entry Control Ordinance 2022 (Deemed Permission Policy 01-25), only Crown forces and civil servants, people working for or under contract to the Government or the British Antarctic Survey, emergency responders and ships' crews work without an Entry Permit.

sources.title: Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands, Entry Control Ordinance: Permit Application
sources.said: Applications can be made by an individual, or multiple applications can be made on behalf of a number of persons by an authorised person such as travel agent, cruise ship operator or a family member. … Applications should be received and paid for at least 8 days prior to the 1st intended date of arrival (disembarkation) in the Territories. … A work permit is valid for 6 months. Both visitor and work permits can be extended, where justified, for a period of an additional 30 days for visitors and 6 months for a work permit, respectively. … Applications for permits for work only – Details of the contract or other arrangement under which the applicant proposes to work in the Territories … Work Permits – No charge for a 6-month permit.

sources.title: Entry Control Ordinance 2022 (SGSSI Ordinance No. 2 of 2022)
sources.said: in the case of a permit for work, 12 months from the expected date of the permit holder first entering the Territories or the period required to perform the contract or other agreement under which the work is to be done, whichever is the shorter … in the case of a permit for work, by up to 6 months

sources.title: SGSSI Gazette No. 4 (2025), Notice of fee for applications for permit for visit or work
sources.said: with effect from 1 August 2025, the fee for an application for:- (a) a visitor permit is £200; and (b) a work permit is £0 (nil)

sources.title: GSGSSI Policy Paper 01-25 (in force 1 August 2025), Entry Control Ordinance 2022, section 9 – Schedule 2: policy on those persons who do not require an Entry Permit (Deemed Permission), dated 5 June 2025 (saved l4w/files/p1c/GS-deemed.pdf)
sources.said: Section 9 of the 2022 Ordinance sets out those persons who are considered to have “deemed” permission to enter the Territories and so do not require an Entry Permit under Section7 of that ordinance. These are set out in Schedule 2 to the Ordinance. … Part A - Persons who have deemed permission to enter the Territories for work or work-related reasons. 1. Any person who is a member of the naval, military or air forces of the Crown … 4. Any person employed or engaged in the provision of goods or services for the purposes of the Government of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. … It does not cover persons who have received a permit or permission from the Government to undertake work in the Territories that is not for or under contract to the Government. 5. Any person who works for or on behalf of the British Antarctic Survey … Part B - Deemed permission for ships’ crews. … Part C – Persons who have deemed permission for other reasons.

sources.title: GSGSSI, Entry Control Ordinance – Permit Application (saved l4w/files/p1c/GS-entry.html)
sources.said: Applications should be received and paid for at least 8 days prior to the 1st intended date of arrival (disembarkation) in the Territories. … Under section 6(5) of the Entry Control Ordinance 2022, applications made 14 days or less before the first intended date of arrival may only be accepted where it was not reasonably practicable to apply earlier. … no application submitted 3 days or less before arrival will be approved.

note: The Entry Control Ordinance 2022 (in force 1 August 2025) lets a work permit run up to 12 months or the contract's length, whichever is shorter, and be extended by up to 6 months; the Government's page says a work permit is valid for 6 months and extendable by 6. The page's 6 months is held as what is granted. The work permit is free (Gazette notice of 22 July 2025). The Government states no decision time, only that applications must be in and paid at least 8 days before arrival, and none made 3 days or less before arrival is approved. Read 2026-11-04 on the Government's own pages: no performer works without an Entry Permit; no decision time is published, only that an application must be in and paid at least 8 days before arrival.
